summary: xAI added a workflows feature to Grok Build that lets a single request fan out across up to 1,024 parallel background agents, verify their outputs, and return a consolidated report.

mechanisms.reason: The lab describes a system feature that fans work out across hundreds of parallel autonomous agents and runs them in the background to completion.
mechanisms.quote: orchestration scripts that fan a task out across hundreds of parallel agents, verify the results, and report back in one background run.

mechanisms.reason: A single task can now spawn up to 1,024 concurrent agents, multiplying the number of model calls issued per task.
mechanisms.quote: Runs get a budget of 128 agents, and up to 1,024 for big jobs.

practices.reason: The document describes a concrete, implementable pattern for decomposing a task into phases, fanning it across agents, and adding adversarial verification before synthesis.
practices.quote: Grok plans the task as a small script: the phases of work, the agents in each phase, and how their results roll up. Each agent starts with a clean, focused context, and the plan can build in checks a single pass can't, like independent skeptics verifying every finding before it reaches the final report.

practices.reason: Saved workflows become reusable slash commands shared via team or user config directories, a new interface convention teams could adopt but not a required migration.
practices.quote: Each saved workflow becomes its own slash command that takes arguments, so once you keep the PR review from the demo above, the next review is just /pr-review 5137 .

notable_reason: A concrete, lab-stated capability for scaling a single task across up to 1,024 background agents is a meaningful marker of how far agentic orchestration is being pushed in production tooling.
